name: vikasana-systems-website
description: Public website for VIKASANA Systems Private Limited. Static, client-rendered, no server component.

scripts.build:seo: npm run sitemap && npm run build && npm run seo:heads
scripts.verify: npm run lint && npm run test:ci && npm run links && npm run copy && npm run render && npm run build:seo && npm run check:artifact && npm run smoke && npm run contrast

//scripts: TWO WAYS TO RUN THE TESTS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHETHER THE PROCESS ENDS.
`test` is bare `craco test`, which is react-scripts' watcher. That is the right
default at a keyboard and the wrong one inside anything that has to finish:
a watching runner in a chain does not fail, it hangs, which costs a CI timeout
instead of a red build and tells you nothing about why. `test:ci` adds
`test` is deliberately left bare rather than made CI-safe, because
the flag through an npm script that already sets it is how a config comes to
disagree with itself. One knob, one owner.
The unit tests run SECOND in `verify`, straight after lint and before anything
that touches the filesystem or the network. They are the fastest signal in the
chain — under three seconds against roughly four minutes for build:seo — and
there is no reason to produce an artefact before discovering that a pure
function regressed. Order the chain by cost, cheapest first.
//dependencies: Runtime dependencies are pinned to exact versions, not ranges. A caret on a
build that ships to a defence customer means the artefact is not reproducible
from the manifest alone; the lockfile is then the only record of what shipped.
gsap carried the project's last caret ('^3.15.0') and has been pinned.
react-scripts is a devDependency. It is a build tool: it contributes nothing to
the bundle, and having it under `dependencies` made `npm audit --omit=dev`
report the whole webpack-4-era transitive tree as production surface. The
installCommand in vercel.json is a plain `npm ci`, which installs devDependencies,
so the build is unaffected.
Removed in the 3 September 2026 hardening pass:
dotenv                   — craco.config.js required it to re-read a .env file
that Create React App has already loaded through
config/env.js before craco is read.
eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y   — both are dependencies of eslint-config-react-app.
eslint-plugin-react-hooks  Declaring them again at the top level, at a MAJOR
version the config does not accept (react-hooks 5.x
against its ^4.3.0), forced npm to install a second
nested copy. Two copies of one plugin resolved by
different paths is what makes ESLint abort with
'Plugin "react-hooks" was conflicted between…' —
a hard build failure, and the reason craco.config.js
carries a comment about it.
engines.node was raised from >=18.18 to >=20. Node 18 reached end of life in
April 2025 and nothing in this project's pipeline runs it — CI pins 22 in
verify.yml and Vercel builds on 22. The floor also has to move because the
patched serialize-javascript below declares node >=20; leaving the old floor
would have made this manifest claim support for a runtime its own build chain
cannot start on. There is no .npmrc and engine-strict is off, so npm would only
have warned — which is precisely how a manifest comes to state something false.
//overrides: These were previously declared under a `resolutions` key. `resolutions` is a Yarn
field and is silently ignored by npm; this project uses package-lock.json, so every
pin below was inert. Verified: svgo pulled nth-check@1.0.2 (ReDoS, GHSA-rp65-9cf3-cjxr)
despite a `resolutions` entry claiming 2.0.1. Renamed to `overrides`, which npm honours.
Every entry here patches a build-time package. None of them reach the shipped
bundle — react-scripts 5.0.1 has had no release since December 2021 and pins a
webpack-4-era tree, so this block is the only way to clear those advisories
short of leaving Create React App.
A PIN IS A SNAPSHOT OF A JUDGEMENT, NOT A FIX. It records the version that was
clean on the day it was written. Advisories are published against versions that
already exist, so a pin that cleared an advisory last quarter can be the thing
carrying one this quarter — and nothing in the manifest changes when that
happens. The block goes on looking correct and the audit goes on getting worse.
That is not hypothetical. The previous version of this paragraph claimed the
block was 'the only way to clear those advisories'. By 23 September 2026 it had
stopped clearing them: `npm audit` reported 133 (2 low, 11 moderate, 120 high)
with every pin below faithfully applied. The sharpest single case was nanoid.
It was pinned at 3.3.11 while postcss 8.5.26 — the consumer this project pinned
postcss to on purpose — declares nanoid ^3.3.17. The override was holding the
tree BELOW its own consumer's floor, and roughly a hundred of the 120 highs were
postcss and its ~90 plugin packages cascading from that one package. Raising one
line took the full tree to 0.
After this pass: `npm audit` reports 0, and `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=low`
reports 0 as it always has. RE-RUN BOTH ON EVERY DEPENDENCY CHANGE AND AT LEAST
QUARTERLY. Read the numbers rather than the block; the block cannot tell you it
has gone stale.
How a version is chosen here. Where the consumer's own declared range already
admits the patched release, take the latest in that major — nanoid 3.3.19 rather
than the minimum-clearing 3.3.18 — because the extra patches are free and the
pin lasts longer before it rots again. Where the pin has to cross a major and
override a consumer's declared range, take the LOWEST version that clears the
advisory and verify the call site by hand. Two entries do that: uuid 11.1.1
against sockjs's declared ^8.3.2 (sockjs calls only `require('uuid').v4()` with
no arguments, and uuid 11 exports v4 from its CJS build), and @tootallnate/once
2.0.1 against http-proxy-agent 4.0.1's declared `1` (v2 sets __esModule and
exports.default, which is exactly what that caller's __importDefault expects).
Flat keys apply to every occurrence in the tree, including transitive ones, and
that is usually what is wanted. js-yaml is the exception and shows why the
scoped form exists. The tree needs 4.3.2 for eslint and @eslint/eslintrc, but
@istanbuljs/load-nyc-config calls yaml.safeLoad, which js-yaml 4 removed — a flat
4.3.2 would clear the advisory and break coverage runs at the same time. The
nested entry pins that one subtree to 3.15.2, the patched tail of the 3.x line.
npm applies the most specific matching rule, so the two coexist.
serialize-javascript is the one pin with a cost outside this block. Clearing the
RCE (GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq, <=7.0.2) and the CPU-exhaustion DoS (GHSA-qj8w-gfj5-8c6v,
<7.0.5) requires the 7.x line, which declares node >=20. There is no 6.x patch.
engines.node moved with it; see the note under //dependencies.
See docs/DEPENDENCIES.md for the artefact triage. Its advisory counts predate
this pass and need updating.
